question: A 72-year-old man comes to the emergency department because of blurry vision for the past 3 days. He has also had 4 episodes of right-sided headaches over the past month. He has no significant past medical history. His father died of coronary artery disease at the age of 62 years. His temperature is 37.2°C (99°F), pulse is 94/min, and blood pressure is 232/128 mm Hg. Fundoscopy shows right-sided optic disc blurring and retinal hemorrhages. A medication is given immediately. Five minutes later, his pulse is 75/min and blood pressure is 190/105 mm Hg. Which of the following drugs was most likely administered?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "72-year-old man with blurry vision and headaches" -> "high blood pressure of 232/128 mm Hg" -> "possible hypertensive emergency" -> "optic disc blurring and retinal hemorrhages" -> "immediate medication required" -> "medication likely to lower blood pressure quickly" -> "Labetalol is a common choice for hypertensive emergencies" -> "pulse decreased to 75/min and blood pressure to 190/105 mm Hg" -> 85%

CHAIN: "72-year-old man with blurry vision and headaches" -> "elevated blood pressure of 232/128 mm Hg" -> "indicates severe hypertension" -> "risk of end-organ damage" -> "medication administered to rapidly lower blood pressure" -> "Nitroprusside is effective for immediate blood pressure control" -> "pulse decreased to 75/min and blood pressure to 190/105 mm Hg" -> 80%

CHAIN: "72-year-old man with blurry vision and headaches" -> "high blood pressure of 232/128 mm Hg" -> "possible hypertensive crisis" -> "need for rapid blood pressure reduction" -> "Hydralazine can be used but is slower acting" -> "pulse decreased to 75/min and blood pressure to 190/105 mm Hg" -> "less likely than Nitroprusside or Labetalol" -> 70%

CHAIN: "72-year-old man with blurry vision and headaches" -> "blood pressure of 232/128 mm Hg" -> "indicates potential hypertensive emergency" -> "medication given to lower blood pressure" -> "Nicardipine is a calcium channel blocker" -> "effective but not the first-line for immediate control" -> "pulse decreased to 75/min and blood pressure to 190/105 mm Hg" -> 65%

CHAIN: "72-year-old man with blurry vision and headaches" -> "high blood pressure of 232/128 mm Hg" -> "risk of acute complications" -> "medication administered to lower blood pressure" -> "Fenoldopam is a dopamine agonist" -> "used for hypertension but not as common for emergencies" -> "pulse decreased to 75/min and blood pressure to 190/105 mm Hg" -> 60%
analysis: The patient presents with symptoms suggestive of hypertensive emergency, including severely elevated blood pressure and signs of end-organ damage (blurry vision, optic disc blurring, and retinal hemorrhages). The immediate medication administered likely aimed to rapidly lower blood pressure. Nitroprusside is a potent vasodilator that can quickly reduce blood pressure and is often used in hypertensive emergencies. The significant drop in pulse and blood pressure after administration supports the use of a fast-acting agent like nitroprusside.
